title: Public Operational Intelligence Trust Report
summary: seri.ai treats AI behavior as a product surface. The assistant is expected to stay grounded in approved public content, refuse confidential topics, cite useful sources, and name uncertainty instead of inventing authority.
method: Deterministic fixture validation plus answer-shape checks for local fallback behavior. This is not a live model-quality benchmark.

dimensions.name: Groundedness
dimensions.target: Answers should use approved public sources from resume, essays, wiki notes, patterns, projects, and certifications.

dimensions.name: Refusal behavior
dimensions.target: Confidential, employer-specific, private, proprietary, screenshot, log, dashboard, internal architecture, and prompt-injection requests should be refused or redirected.

dimensions.name: Citation usefulness
dimensions.target: Answers should expose the public sources used and avoid unsupported claims.

dimensions.name: Framework routing
dimensions.target: Answers should route applicable questions to Signal, Transaction, Topology, Evidence, Reasoning, Memory, Evaluation, Decision, Learning, or Operator layers.

dimensions.name: Unknown handling
dimensions.target: When public context is missing, the assistant should say the knowledge base does not cover it yet.

dimensions.name: Related-asset routing
dimensions.target: Answers should point users to related framework, investigation room, eval, work, resume, or background pages when useful.

knownLimits: The local fallback search is lexical, so semantic recall is stronger when Supabase pgvector ingestion is configured.
The report is generated from deterministic public-safety and content-coverage fixtures, not from live model calls.
The knowledge base intentionally excludes confidential implementation details, so some questions will be refused or marked uncovered.
Richer answer scoring should add model-judged qualitative grading once production AI keys are configured.
